target.engineering_description: SOP-28 IC package body: 11.3mm x 21mm x 3mm rectangular block, with sketch plane slightly rotated (~0.28 deg) about Y axis. Same package family as index 4 but larger and rotated in assembly.

frame._doc_rotated: Frame is ROTATED ~0.28deg about Y axis (not axis-aligned). u_dir and v_dir have small off-axis components (~0.0049). This is the critical test for vertex_projection: axis-aligned bbox would give DIFFERENT (larger) spans than the true frame-axis spans. Only vertex_projection onto u/v/w yields the correct design dimensions.

world_bbox_estimate._doc: Rotated frame: world spans are LARGER than frame spans. along_x = 21*cos(0.28deg)+11.3*sin(0.28deg) ≈ 21.0004+0.055 ≈ 21.055? Recompute: the body's world-X extent = |width_v*v_x| + |length_u*u_x| = 21*0.99999 + 11.3*0.00489 ≈ 21.055. along_z = |width_v*v_z| + |length_u*u_z| = 21*0.00489 + 11.3*0.99999 ≈ 11.403. GT bbox confirms: x[-0.565,0.565]=1.13cm? No GT says x[-0.565,0.565] -> 1.13cm=11.3mm along_x. Hmm GT along_x=11.3 not 21.055. See warning.

warnings: Unit conversion cm->mm (x10): length 1.13cm->11.3mm, width 2.1cm->21mm, extrude 0.3cm->3mm.

ROTATED FRAME (critical test): u_dir/v_dir NOT axis-aligned (off-axis ~0.0049, ~0.28deg rotation about Y). This is the case where axis-aligned bbox FAILS and vertex_projection is REQUIRED. KQP must project vertices onto the actual u/v/w vectors, not world axes.

WORLD BBOX ANOMALY: GT bbox = x[-0.565,0.565] y[0,0.3] z[-1.05,1.05] (cm) -> along_x=11.3mm, along_y=3mm, along_z=21mm. But with rotated frame, world bbox should be LARGER than frame spans (rotation inflates axis-aligned bbox). GT shows along_x=11.3=length_u and along_z=21=width_v EXACTLY, implying NO inflation. This means either (a) the rotation is so tiny (0.28deg) that inflation < tolerance, or (b) GT bbox is computed in sketch-local frame not world. LIKELY (a): 0.28deg inflation = 21*sin(0.28deg)=0.103mm, within 0.01mm tol? No, 0.103 > 0.01. So GT bbox may be sketch-local. Compiler should NOT rely on GT world bbox for rotated frames; use vertex_projection on actual STEP geometry.
world_bbox_estimate above is APPROXIMATE and may not match GT; marked informational only (derived, non-authoritative).
